newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds await asset-backed bond, FFR Pfandbrief.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds await asset-backed bond, FFR Pfandbrief.

text.p: The primary market started the week quietly with the announcement by British Prime Minister John Major that an election would take place on Thursday, May 1 seen curbing sterling supply.
But a syndicate official at NatWest Capital Markets said a collateralised issue for Housing Association was due to be launched later this week.
The deal is expected to be a five-tranche transaction totalling 926 million stg.
But dealers away from the lead said it would be difficult to launch this bond. "They'll find it tough," a dealer said.

"It will be a choppy period in the run-up to the election and market conditions will not be optimum," a syndicate manager at a British bank said. "International investors will prefer to wait on the sidelines until after the election."

Retail-targeted deals in particular would be inhibited by uncertainty before the election, while institutionally-aimed transactions might be more resilient to the long election campaign period, dealers said.
Other factors that will put a lid on sterling supply are the pound's back-tracking from recent highs against the mark, the Easter holiday and a 10-year gilt auction, traders said.
Meanwhile, Frankfurter Hypothekenbank Centralboden plans to launch the first Pfandbrief denominated in French francs with launch as soon as this week.
The offering -- expected to be a 2.0 billion French franc 12-year Pfandbrief -- will be jointly lead managed by Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley.
Pfandbriefe are bonds backed either by public sector-secured debt or mortgages.
Hypothekenbank will be holding a presentation for investors in Paris on Tuesday. Its Pfandbriefe are rated AAA by Standard & Poor's Corp.
